description_en: A use-after-free flaw was found in vcs_read in drivers/tty/vt/vc_screen.c in vc_screen in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow an attacker with local user access to cause a system crash or leak internal kernel information.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s IP framework for transforming packets (XFRM subsystem). This issue may allow a malicious user with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to directly dereference a NULL pointer in xfrm_update_ae_params(), leading to a possible kernel crash and denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s IP framework for transforming packets (XFRM subsystem). This issue may allow a malicious user with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to cause a 4 byte out-of-bounds read of XFRMA_MTIMER_THRESH when parsing netlink attributes, leading to potential leakage of sensitive heap data to userspace.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the siano smsusb module in the Linux kernel. The bug occurs during device initialization when the siano device is plugged in. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system, causing a denial of service condition.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the cxgb4 driver in the Linux kernel. The bug occurs when the cxgb4 device is detaching due to a possible rearming of the flower_stats_timer from the work queue. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system, causing a denial of service condition.

A flaw was found in the exFAT driver of the Linux kernel. The vulnerability exists in the implementation of the file name reconstruction function, which is responsible for reading file name entries from a directory index and merging file name parts belonging to one file into a single long file name. Since the file name characters are copied into a stack variable, a local privileged attacker could use this flaw to overflow the kernel stack.

IN THE EXTENSION SCRIPT, a SQL Injection vulnerability was found in PostgreSQL if it uses @extowner@, @extschema@, or @extschema:...@ inside a quoting construct (dollar quoting, '', or ""). If an administrator has installed files of a vulnerable, trusted, non-bundled extension, an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege can execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser.

A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in vmxnet3_rq_cleanup in drivers/net/vmxnet3/vmxnet3_drv.c in the networking sub-component in vmxnet3 in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker with normal user privilege to cause a denial of service due to a missing sanity check during cleanup.

A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem of the Linux kernel. A race condition between IPSET_CMD_ADD and IPSET_CMD_SWAP can lead to a kernel panic due to the invocation of `__ip_set_put` on a wrong `set`. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system.

LibTIFF is vulnerable to an integer overflow. This flaw allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly execute an arbitrary code via a crafted tiff image, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel ipv4 stack. The socket buffer (skb) was assumed to be associated with a device before calling __ip_options_compile, which is not always the case if the skb is re-routed by ipvs. This issue may allow a local user with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to crash the system.

A flaw was found in the IPv4 Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) classifier in the Linux kernel. The xprt pointer may go beyond the linear part of the skb, leading to an out-of-bounds read in the `rsvp_classify` function. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system and cause a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel. The nfnl_osf_add_callback function did not validate the user mode controlled opt_num field. This flaw allows a local privileged (CAP_NET_ADMIN) attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds read, leading to a crash or information disclosure.

A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel. The xt_u32 module did not validate the fields in the xt_u32 structure. This flaw allows a local privileged attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds read by setting the size fields with a value beyond the array boundaries, leading to a crash or information disclosure.

A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel. The sctp_mt_check did not validate the flag_count field. This flaw allows a local privileged (CAP_NET_ADMIN) attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds read, leading to a crash or information disclosure.

A vulnerability was discovered in Samba, where the flaw allows SMB clients to truncate files, even with read-only permissions when the Samba VFS module "acl_xattr" is configured with "acl_xattr:ignore system acls = yes". The SMB protocol allows opening files when the client requests read-only access but then implicitly truncates the opened file to 0 bytes if the client specifies a separate OVERWRITE create disposition request. The issue arises in configurations that bypass kernel file system permissions checks, relying solely on Samba's permissions.

A path traversal vulnerability was identified in Samba when processing client pipe names connecting to Unix domain sockets within a private directory. Samba typically uses this mechanism to connect SMB clients to remote procedure call (RPC) services like SAMR LSA or SPOOLSS, which Samba initiates on demand. However, due to inadequate sanitization of incoming client pipe names, allowing a client to send a pipe name containing Unix directory traversal characters (../). This could result in SMB clients connecting as root to Unix domain sockets outside the private directory. If an attacker or client managed to send a pipe name resolving to an external service using an existing Unix domain socket, it could potentially lead to unauthorized access to the service and consequential adverse events, including compromise or service crashes.

A vulnerability was found in Samba's "rpcecho" development server, a non-Windows RPC server used to test Samba's DCE/RPC stack elements. This vulnerability stems from an RPC function that can be blocked indefinitely. The issue arises because the "rpcecho" service operates with only one worker in the main RPC task, allowing calls to the "rpcecho" server to be blocked for a specified time, causing service disruptions. This disruption is triggered by a "sleep()" call in the "dcesrv_echo_TestSleep()" function under specific conditions. Authenticated users or attackers can exploit this vulnerability to make calls to the "rpcecho" server, requesting it to block for a specified duration, effectively disrupting most services and leading to a complete denial of service on the AD DC. The DoS affects all other services as "rpcecho" runs in the main RPC task.

A flaw was found in wildfly-core. A management user could use the resolve-expression in the HAL Interface to read possible sensitive information from the Wildfly system. This issue could allow a malicious user to access the system and obtain possible sensitive information from the system.

A race condition was found in the QXL driver in the Linux kernel. The qxl_mode_dumb_create() function dereferences the qobj returned by the qxl_gem_object_create_with_handle(), but the handle is the only one holding a reference to it. This flaw allows an attacker to guess the returned handle value and trigger a use-after-free issue, potentially leading to a denial of service or privilege escalation.

A flaw was found in the Quarkus Cache Runtime. When request processing utilizes a Uni cached using @CacheResult and the cached Uni reuses the initial "completion" context, the processing switches to the cached Uni instead of the request context. This is a problem if the cached Uni context contains sensitive information, and could allow a malicious user to benefit from a POST request returning the response that is meant for another user, gaining access to sensitive data.

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was found in smbCalcSize in fs/smb/client/netmisc.c in the Linux Kernel. This issue could allow a local attacker to crash the system or leak internal kernel information.

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was found in smb2_dump_detail in fs/smb/client/smb2ops.c in the Linux Kernel. This issue could allow a local attacker to crash the system or leak internal kernel information.

A null pointer dereference vulnerability was found in nft_dynset_init() in net/netfilter/nft_dynset.c in nf_tables in the Linux kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN user privilege to trigger a denial of service.

A flaw was found in Quarkus. This issue occurs when receiving a request over websocket with no role-based permission specified on the GraphQL operation, Quarkus processes the request without authentication despite the endpoint being secured. This can allow an attacker to access information and functionality outside of normal granted API permissions.

A memory disclosure vulnerability was found in PostgreSQL that allows remote users to access sensitive information by exploiting certain aggregate function calls with 'unknown'-type arguments. Handling 'unknown'-type values from string literals without type designation can disclose bytes, potentially revealing notable and confidential information. This issue exists due to excessive data output in aggregate function calls, enabling remote users to read some portion of system memory.

An arithmetic overflow flaw was found in Satellite when creating a new personal access token. This flaw allows an attacker who uses this arithmetic overflow to create personal access tokens that are valid indefinitely, resulting in damage to the system's integrity.

A memory leak problem was found in ctnetlink_create_conntrack in net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to cause a denial of service (DoS) attack due to a refcount overflow.

A flaw was found in CRI-O that involves an experimental annotation leading to a container being unconfined. This may allow a pod to specify and get any amount of memory/cpu, circumventing the kubernetes scheduler and potentially resulting in a denial of service in the node.

A flaw was found in the blkgs destruction path in block/blk-cgroup.c in the Linux kernel, leading to a cgroup blkio memory leakage problem. When a cgroup is being destroyed, cgroup_rstat_flush() is only called at css_release_work_fn(), which is called when the blkcg reference count reaches 0. This circular dependency will prevent blkcg and some blkgs from being freed after they are made offline. This issue may allow an attacker with a local access to cause system instability, such as an out of memory error.

A Null pointer dereference problem was found in ida_free in lib/idr.c in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow an attacker using this library to cause a denial of service problem due to a missing check at a function return.

A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux Kernel. When a disk is removed, bdi_unregister is called to stop further write-back and waits for associated delayed work to complete. However, wb_inode_writeback_end() may schedule bandwidth estimation work after this has completed, which can result in the timer attempting to access the recently freed bdi_writeback.

An out-of-bounds memory read flaw was found in receive_encrypted_standard in fs/smb/client/smb2ops.c in the SMB Client sub-component in the Linux Kernel. This issue occurs due to integer underflow on the memcpy length, leading to a denial of service.

A denial of service vulnerability due to a deadlock was found in sctp_auto_asconf_init in net/sctp/socket.c in the Linux kernel’s SCTP subsystem. This flaw allows guests with local user privileges to trigger a deadlock and potentially crash the system.

A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux Kernel due to a race problem in the unix garbage collector's deletion of SKB races with unix_stream_read_generic() on the socket that the SKB is queued on.

A null pointer dereference flaw was found in the hugetlbfs_fill_super function in the Linux kernel hugetlbfs (HugeTLB pages) functionality. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

A Marvin vulnerability side-channel leakage was found in the RSA decryption operation in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a network attacker to decrypt ciphertexts or forge signatures, limiting the services that use that private key.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NVMe driver. This issue may allow an unauthenticated malicious actor to send a set of crafted TCP packages when using NVMe over TCP, leading the NVMe driver to a NULL pointer dereference in the NVMe driver and causing kernel panic and a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NVMe driver. This issue may allow an unauthenticated malicious actor to send a set of crafted TCP packages when using NVMe over TCP, leading the NVMe driver to a NULL pointer dereference in the NVMe driver, causing kernel panic and a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NVMe driver. This issue may allow an unauthenticated malicious actor to send a set of crafted TCP packages when using NVMe over TCP, leading the NVMe driver to a NULL pointer dereference in the NVMe driver, causing kernel panic and a denial of service.

A vulnerability was reported in the Open vSwitch sub-component in the Linux Kernel. The flaw occurs when a recursive operation of code push recursively calls into the code block. The OVS module does not validate the stack depth, pushing too many frames and causing a stack overflow. As a result, this can lead to a crash or other related issues.
A heap overflow flaw was found in 389-ds-base. This issue leads to a denial of service when writing a value larger than 256 chars in log_entry_attr.

A vulnerability in the Eclipse Vert.x toolkit results in a memory leak due to using Netty FastThreadLocal data structures. Specifically, when the Vert.x HTTP client establishes connections to different hosts, triggering the memory leak. The leak can be accelerated with intimate runtime knowledge, allowing an attacker to exploit this vulnerability. For instance, a server accepting arbitrary internet addresses could serve as an attack vector by connecting to these addresses, thereby accelerating the memory leak.

A vulnerability in the Eclipse Vert.x toolkit causes a memory leak in TCP servers configured with TLS and SNI support. When processing an unknown SNI server name assigned the default certificate instead of a mapped certificate, the SSL context is erroneously cached in the server name map, leading to memory exhaustion. This flaw allows attackers to send TLS client hello messages with fake server names, triggering a JVM out-of-memory error.

A flaw was found in Keycloak, where it does not properly validate URLs included in a redirect. This issue could allow an attacker to construct a malicious request to bypass validation and access other URLs and sensitive information within the domain or conduct further attacks. This flaw affects any client that utilizes a wildcard in the Valid Redirect URIs field, and requires user interaction within the malicious URL.

A flaw was found in Keycloak's OIDC component in the "checkLoginIframe," which allows unvalidated cross-origin messages. This flaw allows attackers to coordinate and send millions of requests in seconds using simple code, significantly impacting the application's availability without proper origin validation for incoming messages.
A flaw was found in coredns. This issue could lead to invalid cache entries returning due to incorrectly implemented caching.
A vulnerability was found in jberet-core logging. An exception in 'dbProperties' might display user credentials such as the username and password for the database-connection.

A flaw was found in the github.com/containers/image library. This flaw allows attackers to trigger unexpected authenticated registry accesses on behalf of a victim user, causing resource exhaustion, local path traversal, and other attacks.

A vulnerability was found in Satellite. When running a remote execution job on a host, the host's SSH key is not being checked. When the key changes, the Satellite still connects it because it uses "-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no". This flaw can lead to a man-in-the-middle attack (MITM), denial of service, leaking of secrets the remote execution job contains, or other issues that may arise from the attacker's ability to forge an SSH key. This issue does not directly allow unauthorized remote execution on the Satellite, although it can leak secrets that may lead to it.

A vulnerability was found in Undertow, where URL-encoded request paths can be mishandled during concurrent requests on the AJP listener. This issue arises because the same buffer is used to decode the paths for multiple requests simultaneously, leading to incorrect path information being processed. As a result, the server may attempt to access the wrong path, causing errors such as "404 Not Found" or other application failures. This flaw can potentially lead to a denial of service, as legitimate resources become inaccessible due to the path mix-up.

A vulnerability was found in Undertow where the ProxyProtocolReadListener reuses the same StringBuilder instance across multiple requests. This issue occurs when the parseProxyProtocolV1 method processes multiple requests on the same HTTP connection. As a result, different requests may share the same StringBuilder instance, potentially leading to information leakage between requests or responses. In some cases, a value from a previous request or response may be erroneously reused, which could lead to unintended data exposure. This issue primarily results in errors and connection termination but creates a risk of data leakage in multi-request environments.

A flaw was found in Go. When FIPS mode is enabled on a system, container runtimes may incorrectly handle certain file paths due to improper validation in the containers/common Go library. This flaw allows an attacker to exploit symbolic links and trick the system into mounting sensitive host directories inside a container. This issue also allows attackers to access critical host files, bypassing the intended isolation between containers and the host system.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. Certain endpoints in Keycloak's admin REST API allow low-privilege users to access administrative functionalities. This flaw allows users to perform actions reserved for administrators, potentially leading to data breaches or system compromise.

A vulnerability was found in Podman, Buildah, and CRI-O. A symlink traversal vulnerability in the containers/storage library can cause Podman, Buildah, and CRI-O to hang and result in a denial of service via OOM kill when running a malicious image using an automatically assigned user namespace (`--userns=auto` in Podman and Buildah). The containers/storage library will read /etc/passwd inside the container, but does not properly validate if that file is a symlink, which can be used to cause the library to read an arbitrary file on the host.

A vulnerability was found in Foreman's loader macros introduced with report templates. These macros may allow an authenticated user with permissions to view and create templates to read any field from Foreman's database. By using specific strings in the loader macros, users can bypass permissions and access sensitive information.

A log spoofing flaw was found in the Tuned package due to improper sanitization of some API arguments. This flaw allows an attacker to pass a controlled sequence of characters; newlines can be inserted into the log. Instead of the 'evil' the attacker could mimic a valid TuneD log line and trick the administrator. The quotes '' are usually used in TuneD logs citing raw user input, so there will always be the ' character ending the spoofed input, and the administrator can easily overlook this. This logged string is later used in logging and in the output of utilities, for example, `tuned-adm get_instances` or other third-party programs that use Tuned's D-Bus interface for such operations.

A vulnerability was found in CRI-O, where it can be requested to take a checkpoint archive of a container and later be asked to restore it. When it does that restoration, it attempts to restore the mounts from the restore archive instead of the pod request. As a result, the validations run on the pod spec, verifying that the pod has access to the mounts it specifies are not applicable to a restored container. This flaw allows a malicious user to trick CRI-O into restoring a pod that doesn't have access to host mounts. The user needs access to the kubelet or cri-o socket to call the restore endpoint and trigger the restore.

A security issue was discovered in the LRA Coordinator component of Narayana. When Cancel is called in LRA, an execution time of approximately 2 seconds occurs. If Join is called with the same LRA ID within that timeframe, the application may crash or hang indefinitely, leading to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the HAL Console in the Wildfly component, which does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output used as a web page that is served to other users. The attacker must be authenticated as a user that belongs to management groups “SuperUser”, “Admin”, or “Maintainer”.

A vulnerability was found in CRI-O. A path traversal issue in the log management functions (UnMountPodLogs and LinkContainerLogs) may allow an attacker with permissions to create and delete Pods to unmount arbitrary host paths, leading to node-level denial of service by unmounting critical system directories.

A flaw was found in openshift-gitops-operator-container. The openshift.io/cluster-monitoring label is applied to all namespaces that deploy an ArgoCD CR instance, allowing the namespace to create a rogue PrometheusRule. This issue can have adverse effects on the platform monitoring stack, as the rule is rolled out cluster-wide when the label is applied.

A flaw was found in npm-serialize-javascript. The vulnerability occurs because the serialize-javascript module does not properly sanitize certain inputs, such as regex or other JavaScript object types, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code. This code could be executed when deserialized by a web browser, causing Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. This issue is critical in environments where serialized data is sent to web clients, potentially compromising the security of the website or web application using this package.

A flaw was found in the 389-ds-base LDAP Server. This issue occurs when issuing a Modify DN LDAP operation through the ldap protocol, when the function return value is not tested and a NULL pointer is dereferenced. If a privileged user performs a ldap MODDN operation after a failed operation, it could lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) or system crash.

A flaw was found in the X server's request handling. Non-zero 'bytes to ignore' in a client's request can cause the server to skip processing another client's request, potentially leading to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in Podman. In a Containerfile or Podman, data written to RUN --mount=type=bind mounts during the podman build is not discarded. This issue can lead to files created within the container appearing in the temporary build context directory on the host, leaving the created files accessible.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An offline session continues to be valid when the offline_access scope is removed from the client. The refresh token is accepted and you can continue to request new tokens for the session. As it can lead to a situation where an administrator removes the scope, and assumes that offline sessions are no longer available, but they are.

A flaw was identified in the X.Org X server’s X Keyboard (Xkb) extension where improper bounds checking in the XkbSetCompatMap() function can cause an unsigned short overflow. If an attacker sends specially crafted input data, the value calculation may overflow, leading to memory corruption or a crash.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland when processing X11 Present extension notifications. Improper error handling during notification creation can leave dangling pointers that lead to a use-after-free condition. This can cause memory corruption or a crash, potentially allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service.

A flaw was discovered in the X.Org X server’s X Keyboard (Xkb) extension when handling client resource cleanup. The software frees certain data structures without properly detaching related resources, leading to a use-after-free condition. This can cause memory corruption or a crash when affected clients disconnect.

A flaw was found in Undertow that can cause remote denial of service attacks. When the server uses the FormEncodedDataDefinition.doParse(StreamSourceChannel) method to parse large form data encoding with application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the method will cause an OutOfMemory issue. This flaw allows unauthorized users to cause a remote denial of service (DoS) attack.

A flaw was found in the 389-ds-base server. A heap buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the `schema_attr_enum_callback` function within the `schema.c` file. This occurs because the code incorrectly calculates the buffer size by summing alias string lengths without accounting for additional formatting characters. When a large number of aliases are processed, this oversight can lead to a heap overflow, potentially allowing a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE).

n authorization flaw in Foreman's GraphQL API allows low-privileged users to access metadata beyond their assigned permissions. Unlike the REST API, which correctly enforces access controls, the GraphQL endpoint does not apply proper filtering, leading to an authorization bypass.

A flaw was found in rubyipmi, a gem used in the Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) component of Red Hat Satellite. An authenticated attacker with host creation or update permissions could exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious username for the BMC interface. This could lead to remote code execution (RCE) on the system.

A flaw was found in the Katello plugin for Red Hat Satellite. This vulnerability, caused by improper sanitization of user-provided input, allows a remote attacker to inject arbitrary SQL commands into the sort_by parameter of the /api/hosts/bootc_images API endpoint. This can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering database errors, and potentially enable Boolean-based Blind SQL injection, which could allow an attacker to extract sensitive information from the database.

A flaw was found in Corosync. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit a wrong return value vulnerability in the Corosync membership commit token sanity check by sending a specially crafted User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet. This can lead to an out-of-bounds read, causing a denial of service (DoS) and potentially disclosing limited memory contents

A flaw was found in Corosync. An integer overflow vulnerability in Corosync's join message sanity validation allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to send crafted User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packets. This can cause the service to crash, leading to a denial of service. This vulnerability specifically affects Corosync deployments configured to use totemudp/totemudpu mode.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. This out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the XKB geometry processing, specifically within the `CheckSetGeom()` and `XkbAddGeomKeyAlias` functions, allows an attacker to read uninitialized or out-of-bounds memory. An attacker with a connection to the X11 server, either locally or remotely, can exploit this without user interaction. This could lead to the disclosure of memory contents or cause a denial of service by crashing the server.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. This vulnerability, an out-of-bounds read, affects the XKB (X Keyboard Extension) modifier map handling. An attacker with access to the X11 server can exploit this by sending a malformed request, which causes the server to read beyond its intended memory boundaries. This can lead to the exposure of sensitive information or cause the server to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in Samba’s vfs_worm module. The module is intended to provide write-once, read-many (WORM) protections by preventing modification of files after a configurable grace period. Due to insufficient validation during rename operations, an authenticated user with write access to a share could overwrite a protected file by renaming a newly created file over the existing WORM-protected file.

A flaw was found in OpenShift Container Platform. Completed pods with restartPolicy: Never do not count toward ResourceQuota pod limits, and Kubernetes events are not quota-scoped. A non-privileged user who can create pods in a namespace can exploit this to generate a large volume of events that accumulate in etcd, causing API server performance degradation across the cluster.

An out-of-bounds read flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland in __glXDisp_ChangeDrawableAttributes(). A wrong size validation check can read a client-controlled number of bytes, exceeding the request buffer, leading to information disclosure. A write path also exists but requires byte-swapped clients which is disabled by default.

A use-after-free flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland in CreateSaverWindow(). A client can trigger a use-after-free read after changing window attributes and forcing the screen saver, leading to information disclosure.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. The dereference control plugin does not check for allocation failure before using a BER structure, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash the LDAP server when the system is under memory pressure.

A flaw was found in Foreman. This broken access control vulnerability allows an authenticated user with host-edit permissions to retarget an existing lookup value override to a different host. This is achieved by modifying the match field through nested host attributes, effectively bypassing authorisation checks. The consequence is the potential for unauthorised modification of managed host configurations across different organisational and location boundaries.

A flaw was found in Foreman. An authenticated user with host-edit permissions could exploit a cross-tenant information disclosure vulnerability. This flaw occurs because the taxonomy_scope controller method does not properly validate organization and location IDs from nested request parameters, bypassing existing authorization checks. This allows the user to leak sensitive infrastructure metadata, including subnet topology, IP ranges, gateways, DNS servers, and VLAN IDs, from organizations and locations they are not authorized to access.

A flaw was found in foreman. Authenticated users with 'view_keypairs' permission can bypass taxonomy scoping, allowing them to download private SSH (Secure Shell) keys from other organizations by directly querying key pair IDs. This vulnerability leads to cross-tenant data exposure in multi-tenant deployments, potentially compromising sensitive information.

A flaw was found in Dogtag PKI's ACME responder where the HTTP-01 challenge validator accepts IP address literals as dns identifiers and follows HTTP redirects without validating that the target is a public address. An unauthenticated ACME account holder can exploit this to perform server-side request forgery (SSRF), making the Dogtag server send HTTP GET requests to internal network services. With the InMemory database backend, the response body of internal targets is disclosed to the attacker through the ACME challenge error.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. An unauthenticated remote attacker can inject LDAP search filters into the CleanAllRUV replication status-check extended operation. Because the handler performs the search against cn=config with elevated replication plugin privileges and returns a boolean match result, the attacker can extract sensitive server configuration metadata, including replication bind DNs and password storage scheme information.

A flaw was found in openshift/oauth-proxy. On paths configured to bypass authentication (skip-auth-regex), the proxy forwards client-supplied identity headers (X-Forwarded-User, X-Forwarded-Email, X-Forwarded-Access-Token) to the upstream application without stripping them. An unauthenticated attacker can inject forged identity headers on whitelisted paths.

A flaw was found in multicluster-global-hub. During a ManagedClusterMigration, the system incorrectly grants all managed hubs read access to a shared communication topic. This allows a compromised managed hub to intercept and collect sensitive bootstrap kubeconfigs, which contain API server tokens intended for other hubs. These tokens have an extended validity of approximately 9.86 years, significantly increasing the risk of unauthorized access and information disclosure to other managed clusters.

A flaw was found in WildFly Elytron. Password hashing and verification normalize input with Unicode NFKC, which can collapse fullwidth characters to ASCII equivalents. A remote attacker can more easily guess affected passwords by using an ASCII-only dictionary against accounts whose passwords were intended to include those non-ASCII characters, leading to unauthorized access.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The template revision endpoint does not enforce object-level authorization when retrieving an audited template revision. An authenticated, low privileged user with a template-related permission, such as view_ptables, can obtain historical template contents belonging to another organization or location by supplying the corresponding audit ID. This can result in unauthorized disclosure of historical template contents, which may contain sensitive configuration information, credentials, or other secrets. The REST API revision endpoints correctly restrict this lookup.

A flaw was found in the Dynamic Client Registration service of Keycloak, an open-source identity and access management solution. The issue occurs when a user with the view-clients role accesses the client registration endpoint to retrieve client details. Due to a failure to mask sensitive information, the service returns the client's confidential secret in cleartext. This could allow a read-only administrator to obtain full access to the affected client's account and potentially escalate their privileges within the realm.

A flaw was found in RESTEasy's CorsFilter, which, when configured to allow all origins ("*"), reflects the request's Origin header back in the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permissive cross-origin policy allows a malicious website to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read authenticated responses from a victim's session, resulting in a loss of confidentiality.

A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 HpackEncoder. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames with a very large MAX_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE. This causes the HpackEncoder to store an excessive number of unique headers, leading to increased CPU usage and memory consumption, ultimately resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 stack. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to inject prohibited characters, such as NUL, Line Feed, and Carriage Return, into HTTP/2 header field values due to insufficient validation. When these values cross an HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 translation boundary, they can be exploited for request smuggling, header injection, or response splitting. This could lead to unauthorized access, data manipulation, or other security bypasses.

A flaw was found in GCC. When an application calls the erase_if function on a binary heap priority queue in libstdc++, the library reallocates storage but fails to update its internal entry pointer. An attacker capable of triggering this operation can exploit this use-after-free condition, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) via an application crash or potential memory corruption.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The foreman-tail utility is vulnerable to OS command injection due to the unsafe use of the eval command. The script takes user-supplied arguments and incorporates them directly into a string that is then executed by eval to expand file paths. Because the input is not sanitized or quoted, a local attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g., ;, &, |) to execute arbitrary system commands.

A flaw was found in rubygem-hammer_cli. A command injection vulnerability exists in Hammer CLI and the Railties (Ruby on Rails) component distributed with Satellite due to the insecure interpolation of the $EDITOR environment variable into the Ruby system() method. By passing a single interpolated string to system(), the application invokes a system shell (/bin/sh) that interprets shell metacharacters (e.g., ;, |, &).

A flaw has been found in **permission filters** in the **foreman** package. The API loads a filter by its identifier and does not apply the search limit on the caller's permission. A low-privileged network attacker or user must already be allowed to delete filters for one role only. They can delete filters that belong to other unlocked roles. Those other roles then lose the access the deleted filters had granted.

A flaw was found in the management interface of the Quarkus framework, specifically within the quarkus-vertx-http component. The issue occurs when the framework incorrectly combines the management root path with specific permission rules, leading to a situation where security policies are applied to the wrong internal paths. As a result, an attacker can bypass intended authorization checks and gain unauthorized access to sensitive management endpoints.

A flaw was found in the SAML HTTP-Redirect binding implementation of Keycloak. The issue occurs because the server processes percent-encoded parameter names (like %53AMLResponse) while the signature verification logic only checks literal parameter names. An attacker can use this discrepancy to provide a crafted, unsigned SAML message that the server processes instead of a legitimately signed one, leading to full account takeover of federated users.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak server's client management component. When a client is created or imported with authorization services enabled, the system fails to properly clear an internal session attribute used during the setup process. This allows an authenticated attacker with client management permissions to bypass security controls and upload a malicious JavaScript policy, which is then executed on the server when an authorization request is made. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to run arbitrary code on the server, potentially compromising the entire system.

A flaw was found in ansible-core's ansible.builtin.git module. The module
invokes git (ls-remote, clone, fetch) with the repository URL as a positional
argument and without a "--" separator, so a repository URL that begins with a
dash is interpreted by git as a command-line option. A caller that passes an
attacker-controlled repository URL to the module can trigger argument
injection (for example --upload-pack/--exec), resulting in arbitrary command
execution on the host running the module.

Fluxion before 6.39 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the fluxion.sh target scanner, which decodes access point ESSIDs with eval after escaping only single quotes. Attackers within Wi-Fi range can broadcast an access point with a crafted SSID to execute commands as root when the operator scans or selects it.

A missing authorization check has been found in the user_mail_notifications function in mail_notifications_controller.rb of the mail notification API in the foreman package. The action returns another user's notification settings when only the generic view permission for mail notifications is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can view mail notifications can request any user id and read that user's subscription choices and stored mail search strings.

A missing authorization check has been found in the find_user function in user_aware.rb of the SSH key API in the foreman package. The create action attaches a new public key to the user id in the request without checking that the caller may edit that user. A low-privileged network attacker or user who already holds permission to create SSH keys can add their key to another user's account. That key is then stored with the victim and can be used by features that export that user's SSH keys.

WLA DX 9.7 before 10.8 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in parse_data_blocks() in wlalink/analyze.c that copies section namespaces without length checks. Attackers can supply a crafted object or library file with a namespace longer than 255 bytes or unterminated to overflow the 256-byte stack buffer when linked.

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

dsniff through 2.5a2 contains an integer underflow in decode_sniffer() in decode_sniffer.c that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write past the global obuf buffer. Attackers can send a UDP datagram to port 2001 on a monitored segment with a 4096-byte string, disabling base64_pton bounds checks to corrupt memory and crash dsniff.

Wfuzz through 3.1.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows malicious target servers to inject script by returning crafted links written unescaped into HTML reports. When the links script and html printer are used, attacker-supplied href values close the unquoted anchor tag and execute JavaScript when the operator opens the report.

hping3 through commit 3547c76 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in display_ipopt() that allows remote attackers to overflow the static 40-byte old_rr buffer via a crafted IP Record Route option. Attackers acting as the probed host, on-path, or spoofing the target can send replies with option lengths up to 255 to hping3 running with -G/--rroute, corrupting global memory and crashing hping3.

A **server-side request forgery** flaw has been found in the get_remote_artifact_url() function in pulp_python/app/models.py of the pull-through caching feature in the **pulp_python** package. The function uses the redirect query parameter from the client request as the URL to download. A network attacker or user who can reach the content app of a Python distribution that has a remote can choose that URL. The content app downloads it and returns the response. When the remote has a username and password, the download sends those credentials to the host in the URL. When the remote policy is immediate, the default, or on_demand, the file is saved into the distribution's repository and later clients are served that file. The project name and version come from the file, and the filename comes from the request path. A filename the repository already stores is served from the stored file.

A vulnerability was determined in projectworlds Online Jewellery Shopping System 1.0. The affected element is the function Dashbord_model.searchAdvance of the file /jewllary-shop/application/models/dashbord_model.php of the component Advanced Search. This manipulation of the argument from/to causes sql injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

A vulnerability was identified in itsourcecode Event Management System 1.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file view_event.php. Such manipulation of the argument ID leads to sql injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

A security flaw has been discovered in Tencent RapidJSON up to 1.1.0. This affects the function Writer::WriteString in the library include/rapidjson/writer.h. Performing a manipulation of the argument length results in integer overflow. The attack may be initiated remotely. The patch is named 297637bc0a0f00dc504dbc1a47ebdaa577f8ae19. To fix this issue, it is recommended to deploy a patch.

A weakness has been identified in sgl-project SpecForge 0.2.0. This impacts the function Eagle3DraftModel.load_embedding of the file specforge/modeling/draft/base.py of the component Draft Embedding Loader. Executing a manipulation can lead to path traversal. The attack can only be executed locally. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. This patch is called d8a0d78e071199563ef19d9171052096dec89f71. It is advisable to implement a patch to correct this issue.

The Apache Airflow TaskFlow decorators @task.bash, @task.sql, @task.analytics, @task.kubernetes_cmd and the common.ai decorators (@task.llm, @task.agent, @task.llm_sql, @task.llm_branch, @task.llm_file_analysis, @task.llm_schema_compare) rendered Jinja templates a second time after the task runner had already rendered them, so any value copied into env, op_args, op_kwargs or the returned prompt, command or SQL was evaluated as a template on the worker. An attacker who can only trigger a Dag run (for example a user with trigger permission supplying run conf), or who controls text that a Dag passes into one of these decorators as an argument or prompt (for example a ticket or a downloaded document), could run arbitrary commands on the worker and read connection passwords and Variables, in any deployment that uses an affected decorator in a Dag that passes such input through env, parameters or prompt. Users are recommended to upgrade apache-airflow-providers-standard to 1.22.0, apache-airflow-providers-cncf-kubernetes to 11.0.0, apache-airflow-providers-common-sql to 3.0.0 and apache-airflow-providers-common-ai to 1.2.0 or later.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Cerebras ModelZoo up to d76e028d6a5f784954b1329b3ae44721ca8da36a. Affected is the function StreamingShardedHFReader of the file src/cerebras/modelzoo/tools/checkpoint_converters/streaming_checkpoints.py of the component Checkpoint Converter. Performing a manipulation of the argument room_id results in sql injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made public and could be used.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in KAP ASIAs LottieFiles – JSON Based Animation Lottie & Bodymovin for Elementor <= 1.10.9 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting include-lottie-animation-for-elementor allows Stored XSS.This issue affects LottieFiles – JSON Based Animation Lottie & Bodymovin for Elementor <= 1.10.9 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting: from n/a through 2.0.3.

A security flaw has been discovered in itsourcecode Event Management System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file /admin/manage_event.php. The manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks.

A security vulnerability has been detected in GH05TCREW PentestAgent 0.2.0. This vulnerability affects the function _execute_single of the file pentestagent/agents/base_agent.py of the component Workspace Scope Gate. Such manipulation leads to missing authorization. The attack needs to be performed locally. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

ezdxf through 1.4.5 contains a code injection vulnerability in the dxf2code add-on that allows attackers to inject Python code via unescaped single quotes in DXF table entry names. Attackers can craft a DXF file whose layer, linetype, style, or appid names break out of quoted strings in generated scripts, executing code with the privileges of the user running them.

torchvision before 0.29.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in _extract_tar() that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction directory by supplying crafted tar archives. Attackers controlling archives passed to extract_archive() or download_and_extract_archive() can use .. paths, absolute paths, or symlinks to overwrite Python modules and achieve code execution.

pyfda through 0.9.5 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_filter() that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .npz or .pkl filter files. Attackers can embed a __reduce__ gadget that runs via np.load with allow_pickle=True or pickle.load before validation, executing code with the user's privileges.

JAL (Just Another Ledger) through 2026.11.3 contains an arbitrary file overwrite vulnerability in backup restore that allows attackers to write files by supplying a crafted .tgz backup with a symlink member. Attackers can include a jal.sqlite symlink to an absolute path followed by a regular jal.sqlite member, overwriting files such as shell startup scripts for code execution.

lastversion before 3.6.20 contains a path traversal vulnerability in extract_tar() that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction directory via tar symlink members. Attackers controlling a project's release assets can craft a tarball with a symlink followed by a file beneath it, writing files like usercustomize.py to achieve code execution.

LibreChat 0.7.6 before 0.8.8 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to block the server event loop by uploading a crafted conversation import file to POST /api/convos/import. Attackers can submit many messages with unresolvable parentMessageId values, triggering quadratic processing in cloneMessagesWithTimestamps or adjustTimestampsForOrdering and stalling the Node.js event loop for minutes for all users.

Video Popup Block by WPZOOM 1.1.2 before 1.1.9 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows Contributor-level users to inject markup via unescaped video URL and popup width values. Attackers can store a block whose .mp4 URL or width breaks out of attributes in frontend.js, executing script in the site's origin when users open the popup.

LibreChat 0.7.8 before 0.8.9 contains a race condition vulnerability in checkBalance that allows authenticated users to obtain multiple auto-refill credits by sending concurrent requests. Attackers can send simultaneous chat requests that each pass the unlocked lastRefill check, receiving repeated refillAmount credits and bypassing configured token credit limits.

InternLM LMDeploy 0.9.0 through 0.18.0 contains an unbounded resource allocation vulnerability in the DistServe proxy /distserve/connection_warmup endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory. While a prefill/decode connection is pending, for example after registering a slow node via /nodes/add, repeated warmup requests spawn unbounded wait_for_conn() tasks and sockets until the proxy process is killed.

Docker Sandboxes re-resolves saved mount paths when replacing a sandbox container during kit changes or restarting a sandbox. An attacker able to replace a source ancestor in a shared writable workspace with a symlink can redirect another sandbox's mount to a different host directory, exposing its contents and permitting modification through read-write mounts. The destination must remain accessible to the daemon and allowed by policy where enforced. Saved-mount replay during kit replacement was introduced in version 0.35.0; ordinary restart replay was added in version 0.45.0. This saved-mount replay issue is fixed in version 0.54.0.

A vulnerability was identified in RT-Thread up to 5.3.0. This impacts the function hpm_adc_enabled of the file bsp/hpmicro/libraries/drivers/drv_adc.c of the component HPM ADC Driver. The manipulation of the argument channel leads to improper validation of array index. The attack needs to be performed locally. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The identifier of the patch is fc64f78669b42b35981f97c23c7e952832f3b48b. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

A security flaw has been discovered in RT-Thread up to 5.3.0. Affected is the function davinci_spi_get_prescale of the file bsp/dm365/drivers/spi-davinci.c of the component DM365 SPI Driver. The manipulation of the argument max_hz results in divide by zero. The attack requires a local approach. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The patch is identified as e12183f7b87eddf182b95bf8b400acd626880306. Applying a patch is advised to resolve this issue.

A weakness has been identified in RT-Thread up to 5.3.0. Affected by this vulnerability is the function bl_adc_get_value of the file bsp/bouffalo_lab/libraries/rt_drivers/drv_adc.c of the component Bouffalo ADC Driver. This manipulation of the argument channel causes improper validation of array index. The attack requires local access. Patch name: b3a0eb5e12c6dca8145fc49d76c4785478c9e55b. It is suggested to install a patch to address this issue.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security (ACS). An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit a vulnerability in the login interface's OAuth callback endpoint by crafting a malicious URL. This URL, containing unvalidated `error` and `error_uri` parameters, allows the attacker to display arbitrary error messages, leading to content spoofing. Furthermore, the attacker can redirect victims to malicious domains, effectively performing an open redirect under the guise of the trusted application's user interface.

An **uncontrolled memory allocation** flaw has been found in the smbd_smb2_ioctl_pipe_write_done() function in source3/smbd/smb2_ioctl_named_pipe.c of the SMB2 named-pipe ioctl handling in the samba package. The file server reserves memory for a named-pipe response using a size chosen by the client. It does not keep that size within the maximum the client and the server have already agreed. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can open a named pipe can request a very large response. The file server reserves that memory before it reads the pipe and holds it until the request ends. Repeating this on more connections can exhaust memory and keep the file service unavailable while those requests continue.

A server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw was found in KubeVirt's decentralized live migration. The connectURL field of a VirtualMachineInstanceMigration object is not validated at admission, and the privileged synchronization-controller dials the attacker-specified URL. Connection and DNS errors from the dial are exposed in a condition readable in the tenant's namespace. A user with the kubevirt.io:migrate role (a role designed for tenant delegation) can use this behavior as a blind network-reconnaissance oracle to determine the existence and connectivity of internal hosts and ports from the controller's network vantage, including services isolated from the tenant by network policy. TLS certificate pinning prevents session completion with non-KubeVirt hosts, limiting the impact to information disclosure of internal network topology; no data content, integrity, or availability impact is possible.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability enables information disclosure when the parameterized-scopes feature is enabled. The protocol mapper fails to enforce authorization checks for certain scope parameter types during token and authorization requests. An authenticated remote attacker can exploit this flaw by supplying a crafted scope parameter to retrieve sensitive profile attributes of other users without authorization.

A flaw was found in spice-server. A malicious SPICE client can send a message header declaring an arbitrarily large message body. The server sizes the receive-buffer allocation from this declared size before any message content is received; when the allocation fails, the process hosting the SPICE server terminates abruptly, causing a denial of service for the virtual machine it serves. On hosts with sufficient free memory, the same technique can instead hold large amounts of memory per connection. Exploitation requires network access to the SPICE port; credential requirements depend on the server's authentication configuration.

A vulnerability has been found in stylefeng Guns up to 2.2. Affected by this issue is the function TokenAndPermissionInterceptor.preHandle of the file TokenAndPermissionInterceptor.java of the component JWT Signing. Such manipulation leads to use of hard-coded cryptographic key . It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

Path traversal in TPM device management in Canonical LXD from 4.8 before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a remote authenticated user with project access to recursively delete arbitrary files and directories on the host as root via a crafted device name during instance or device removal.

In LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2, an improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to write and delete files at arbitrary host filesystem paths as root.

 When a custom storage volume is pushed to a LXD daemon, the snapshot names supplied by the migration peer are never validated and are used to build the filesystem path of each received snapshot. This allows an attacker to place attacker-controlled files into any host directory as root, gaining root-level code execution on the host, and to recursively delete an attacker-chosen path.

In LXD before 5.21.0 and 6.10.0, an OS command injection vulnerability allows an authenticated client restricted to a single project to execute arbitrary code as root on the host.

 The raw.dnsmasq bridge network configuration key is not restricted to server administrators and is copied verbatim into the dnsmasq configuration file, so a user whose project keeps the default features.networks=false can have a bridge network created in the default project with an injected dhcp-script directive. This allows an attacker to make the host dnsmasq execute attacker-chosen code as root on a DHCP lease event and fully compromise the host.

Symbolic link following in imported VM backup config drive preparation in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project-scoped permissions to disclose sensitive host files, including LXD server and cluster keys, and overwrite host files as root via importing and starting a VM backup with a symlinked config directory.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in VM disk migration, export, and attach NBD servers in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an unprivileged local user in the host network namespace to read and modify a guest VM's disk and execute code inside the guest via connecting to abstract Unix sockets while an operation is active.

Improper privilege management during container rebuild in Canonical LXD before 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a local user with container permissions to gain root privileges on the host via rebuilding a never-started unprivileged container so it starts without a user namespace or privileged-container hardening.

Path traversal in proxy and CDI GPU device name handling in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, and 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with access to a restricted project permitting proxy or GPU devices to read, overwrite, or delete arbitrary host files as root and terminate host processes via crafted device names containing path traversal sequences.

Improper link resolution in image metadata tarball unpacking in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, and 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with a restricted client certificate to write arbitrary host files as root and execute code on the host via a crafted rootfs symlink in an image metadata tarball.

Exposure of sensitive information in token operation events in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user restricted to a project to gain full server access and cancel pending token operations via capturing certificate or cluster join token secrets broadcast to default project event listeners.

Exposure of sensitive information and missing requestor validation in instance, volume, and snapshot migration operations in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project event or operation read access to read migrating configuration and filesystem data and disrupt the migration via capturing per-connection websocket secrets from operation metadata and racing the migration's data channels.

Configuration injection in virtual machine disk device handling in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with VM creation permissions in a restricted project to bypass low-level VM restrictions and control the root QEMU process via quotes and line breaks in a disk device's guest path.

Exposure of sensitive information in live and stateful migration operations in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project event or operation read access to read a migrating instance's checkpointed runtime state and disrupt the migration via capturing the state connection secret from operation events or queries.

Improper output encoding in Prometheus metrics exposition in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a user controlling a virtual machine to forge host metric labels and break metrics scraping via unescaped guest-controlled filesystem mountpoints and network interface names.

Improper certificate validation in websocket connections in Canonical pylxd before 2.4.3 allows a network attacker to read command stdin and spoof command output via impersonating a remote LXD endpoint.

The Android application "Tokyo Fire Department Official App" contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows a malicious application installed on a user's device to obtain sensitive information from the affected application.

Incorrect authorization in custom storage volume, backup, and storage bucket endpoints in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with a project-restricted certificate or per-object authorization to read, rename, move, replace, or delete other projects' storage resources and bypass cluster group restrictions via missing project or object ownership checks.

Path traversal in container device path resolution and VM disk format detection in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with project access, including an unprivileged local user through lxd-user, to read and modify arbitrary host files or Ceph RBD images and gain root privileges on the host via crafted device paths or QCOW2 backing file references.

Insufficient verification of data authenticity in shared image handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user restricted to a single project to export private images, replace public image contents, remove other projects' images, and pin daemon memory via abusing fingerprint-based image sharing, partial fingerprints, and non-expiring push upload tokens.

Untrusted search path and context handling in host-side instance helpers in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access or root inside an unprivileged container to execute arbitrary code as root on the host, read daemon memory, remount read-only shifted disks as read-write, and disrupt other projects' mounts via file API, SFTP, syscall interception, and disk hot-plug operations.

Incorrect authorization in project restriction enforcement in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to bypass project limits and access forbidden storage pools, volumes, network addresses, and CPU resources via instance moves, backup imports with overrides, received snapshots, or unvalidated volatile keys.

Exposure of sensitive information in API responses, exports, and host-side artifacts in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated lower-privileged user or a local host user to read credentials, private keys, and other projects' metadata and inject arguments into Ceph administration commands via unfiltered endpoints, exported configurations, log files, process command lines, and unvalidated bucket parameters.

Incorrect authorization in NIC, managed network, network zone, and ACL handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user of a restricted project or root inside an instance to manipulate host interfaces and firewall rules, read fragments of root-owned files through error messages, and disrupt or intercept other projects' networks and DNS records via unvalidated device and network configurations.

Improper control of code generation and project restriction enforcement in container configuration handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to execute arbitrary commands as root on the host, crash the daemon, and alter shared bridge DHCP assignments via image-supplied LXC configuration, concurrent rename races during updates, and unvalidated syscall or hardware address settings.

Incorrect authorization in instance, snapshot, and image operations in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project or per-object permissions to read and modify other clients' resources and execute arbitrary code as root on the host via missing entitlement checks on secondary objects and push-mode container migrations.

Incorrect permission assignment for critical resources in rsync transfer sockets, instance storage directories, proxy socket paths, and disk staging mounts in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an unprivileged local user to gain root privileges on the host, read or modify transferred volumes, alter host file permissions, and inject AppArmor rules via connecting to unauthenticated abstract Unix sockets, running setuid binaries, or racing path and mount operations.

Path traversal in backup, image, storage volume, and migration handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and write arbitrary host files as root and exhaust daemon memory via crafted symlinks, unvalidated path components, or oversized metadata.

Incorrect authorization in TLS certificate trust store and revocation handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated client with a restricted or revoked TLS certificate to gain unrestricted administrative access to the server or cluster via trust-lookup races, forwarded cluster identity headers, CA-issued certificate detaching, or stale revocation and session state.

Improper authentication in OIDC bearer token verification in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a remote attacker holding a token signed by the configured identity provider to authenticate to the LXD API and gain unauthorized control or impersonate users via presenting tokens issued for other applications, ID tokens, or unverified email claims.

Incorrect authorization in backup export and network zone read endpoints in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with view-only access to export instance and custom storage volume backups and read network zone TSIG peer keys via endpoints enforcing only view permissions.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in image template handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and overwrite host block and character devices via importing device nodes in an image's templates directory and accessing them through instance template endpoints.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in optimized ZFS backup imports in Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to mount an attacker-controlled filesystem over arbitrary host paths and execute code as root on the host via importing a filesystem ZFS stream declared as a block volume.

Configuration injection in liblxc instance configuration generation in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2, 5.21.10, 5.0.12, 4.0.16 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access or a local user of the LXD user socket to execute arbitrary commands as root on the host via line breaks in instance configuration keys and values.

Authentication bypass by spoofing in bridged NIC MAC filtering in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a privileged user inside an instance sharing a managed bridge to intercept and deny inbound network traffic addressed to a neighbour instance via sending frames with a spoofed source MAC address before filtering drops them.

Improper link resolution before file access in recursive file pull in Canonical LXD before 4.0.15, 5.0.11, 5.21.9, and 6.8 on case-insensitive client filesystems allows an authenticated user with write access to an instance directory or custom volume to write arbitrary files outside the target directory and execute code as the operator via case-variant symlinks.

Improper authentication in the guest API connection handling in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows a root user inside an unisolated instance to impersonate another instance and read its configuration, metadata, and devices across project boundaries via holding open connections across PID wrap-around.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in the instance file transfer API in Canonical LXD before 4.0.16, 5.0.12, 5.21.10, 6.10.2 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and write arbitrary host block or character devices, compromise the host, and hang file transfer requests via importing device nodes or named pipes outside /dev in an image or backup and opening them on a stopped instance.

Exposure of resource to wrong sphere in image and backup metadata handling in Canonical LXD before 6.10.2, 5.21.10, 5.0.12, 4.0.16 allows an authenticated user with restricted project access to read and overwrite arbitrary host files, access other projects' data, and block the daemon via importing device nodes, hard links, symlinks, or named pipes.

A vulnerability was detected in ONNX ONNXMLTools up to 1.16.0. This affects the function get_set_node of the file onnxmltools/utils/visualize.py of the component Model Visualization. The manipulation results in cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A flaw has been found in ONNX ONNXMLTools up to 1.16.0. This impacts the function visualize_model of the file onnxmltools/utils/visualize.py. This manipulation of the argument producer_name causes basic cross site scripting. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A vulnerability has been found in code-projects Simple Laundry System 1.0. This affects an unknown function of the file viewdetailforuser.php. The manipulation of the argument serviceId leads to sql injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

The Sneeit Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in versions up to, and including, 8.7 via the 'callback' parameter of the sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content AJAX action. The handler sneeit_compact_menu_mega_content_callback() is registered on the wp_ajax_nopriv_ hook and passes the attacker-supplied 'callback' value directly into call_user_func() after only a function_exists() check, with the single argument also attacker-controlled via a JSON-decoded 'args' parameter. There is no authentication, no capability check, no nonce, and no allow-list of callable functions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary existing PHP/WordPress functions with controlled arguments.

The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Database for Contact Form 7, WPforms, Elementor forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.5 via the copy_files function. This is due to missing file extension validation in the copy_files function, which accepts attacker-controlled stream wrapper URIs as the file source and derives the destination filename without restricting executable extensions. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The plugin places an .htaccess file in its uploads directory to block PHP execution, but this mitigation is ineffective on Nginx, LiteSpeed in certain configurations, and Apache servers with AllowOverride None, and the file is not restored if deleted.

The Forminator Forms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Account Approval Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.3 via the forminator_replace_custom_form_data() function. This is due to the function expanding the {all_fields} merge tag before {account_approval_link}, so a submitter-supplied field value containing the literal string {account_approval_link} is resolved into the real activation URL, including the secret activation key, in the user confirmation email. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to obtain the activation link for their own pending registration and activate the account via the ?page=account_activation&key= endpoint, bypassing the manual approval configured on the registration form. Exploitation requires a user-registration form with manual approval enabled and a user confirmation email that includes the {all_fields} merge tag (the default template). Note: On WordPress Multisite installations with site registration enabled, the self-activated account also becomes the Administrator of the subsite created during registration.

The Translate WordPress with Weglot 2.0 – Multilingual AI Translation plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the target site to permit anonymous comment posting (comment_registration disabled) and have at least one Weglot destination language active; on sites with comment moderation enabled, an administrator must approve the carrier and trigger comments before the injected script executes for subsequent visitors.

The W3 Total Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.11.0 via deserialization of untrusted input that is injected into the Memcached object cache through request Host header key truncation. This allows authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject a PHP Object. The additional presence of a POP chain (the bundled Guzzle FileCookieJar, reached through the W3TC\CdnEngine_S3 autoload bridge) allows attackers to write arbitrary files and execute code. This requires the Object Cache to be enabled with the Memcached method backed by the pecl memcache extension and Minify to be enabled; using the same key collision, the attacker first escalates from Subscriber to Administrator.
Exim before 4.100.2 allows attackers to send SMTP traffic that triggers a heap out-of-bounds write in expansion code running as root.
